title: The AI gains that gdp misses
contentHtml:
That is a recent essay of mine, published in The Humanist Review of AI.  Excerpt:

One way to think of these matching gains is to say that AI helps consumers get hold of more customized products. The effective, available degree of product variety rises sharply due to AI. But again, that effect is not captured by typical, quality-based adjustments in how GDP is calculated.

Note that new, customized products typically involve higher gains in consumer welfare than older, established products. If there is a new product, or at least a product newly available to you (perhaps for informational reasons), ex ante the effective price of that product to you was infinity. You simply could not get it. But when that product becomes available, typically it does so at a pretty normal price. That is, in essence, a pretty large price decline, and if you value the new product a lot, as I did my Sokolov concert, the gains can be large. It is more difficult to reap comparably large gains by simply purchasing more of an established product that has been in front of you as a buying opportunity for a long period of time.

Here are other essays in the journal, including from Nobel Laureate Philippe Aghion.
